name: Swiss International Typographic Style
description: Swiss International Typographic Style — precision, clarity, grid-based order from the Basel and Zurich schools

foundation.story: Born from the Basel and Zurich schools of the 1950s, Swiss International Style prioritized objective clarity over decorative expression. Designers like Josef Müller-Brockmann and Armin Hofmann established principles of grid-based composition, asymmetric layouts, and sans-serif typography that became the global standard for corporate and informational design.
foundation.philosophy: Sachlichkeit (Objectivity) — form follows function with mathematical precision

seedColors.name: Schwarz
seedColors.tradition: Pure typographic black. The foundation of Swiss poster design and Helvetica specimens.
seedColors.source: Swiss Graphic Design: The Origins and Growth of an International Style, R. Hollis

seedColors.name: Weiss
seedColors.tradition: Paper white. The generous whitespace that gives Swiss design its breathing room.
seedColors.source: Grid Systems in Graphic Design, Josef Müller-Brockmann

seedColors.name: Rot (Signal Red)
seedColors.tradition: The accent of Swiss rail (SBB/CFF), national flag, and Müller-Brockmann concert posters. Pure signal with no ambiguity.
seedColors.source: Swiss Style: The Graphic Design of Swiss International Style

seedColors.name: Mittelgrau
seedColors.tradition: Mid-grey for secondary information hierarchy. Swiss design uses grey to create clear visual levels.
seedColors.source: Typographic Design: Form and Communication, R. Carter

seedColors.name: Hellgrau
seedColors.tradition: Light grey for borders, dividers, and subtle structural elements in grid systems.

seedColors.name: Dunkelblau
seedColors.tradition: Swiss corporate blue. Used in banking, insurance, and institutional communications for trust and authority.
